title: Radiation asymptotics and controlled multipole expansion

items.title: Retarded Maxwell fields for spatially compact smooth histories
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $a,c,\mu_0>0$, let $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$, and let $\rho:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ and $J:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ be jointly $C^\infty$. Suppose $\rho(y,t)=J(y,t)=0$ whenever $|y|>a$ and suppose the continuity equation $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}_yJ=0$ holds everywhere.

Adopt the smooth vacuum Maxwell equations and the retarded, no-free-addition selection as the physical model assumptions. In the SI laboratory convention, define

$$\varphi(x,t):=\frac{\mu_0c^2}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\rho(y,t-|x-y|/c)}{|x-y|}\,dy,\qquad A(x,t):=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{J(y,t-|x-y|/c)}{|x-y|}\,dy.$$

The integrals converge absolutely at every $(x,t)$. The resulting potentials are jointly $C^\infty$ and satisfy $W\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $WA=\mu_0J$, and $\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi=0$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, where $W=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$. Consequently $E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$ and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ are jointly smooth and satisfy the smooth vacuum Maxwell equations for $(\rho,J)$ everywhere. This is the selected retarded solution, with no independent homogeneous field added. No compact support in time is assumed.
items.strategy: localize each arbitrary history to the finite time interval sampled near an observation event, use the compactly supported retarded kernel theorem there, and derive the Lorenz condition from continuity.

references.title: Niklas Beisert, Elektrodynamik, Vorlesungsskript, ETH Zürich 2024 FS, complete 176-page course script
references.locator: §11.2, printed pp. 11.4–11.7 (PDF pp. 124–127): retarded and advanced Green kernels, the sourced wave equations and the retarded-potential construction; the source-history localization used here is proved independently.

references.title: Richard Fitzpatrick, Classical Electromagnetism: An intermediate level course, University of Texas at Austin, complete author-hosted HTML lecture notes
references.locator: Chapter 4, node 50, “Retarded potentials”: the retarded Green-function construction for scalar and vector potentials and its retardation convention; the arbitrary-time-history extension is proved independently.

items.physical_scope: The smooth retarded solution branch of classical vacuum electromagnetism for conserved volume sources supported in one fixed spatial ball at every time, including histories that are not compactly supported in time. The result establishes local finiteness, smoothness, the sourced wave equations, Lorenz gauge and the smooth Maxwell system for the selected retarded potentials. Point, sheet and other singular sources, self-force, radiation reaction, finite-energy claims and empirical claims are excluded.

items.title: Radiation data at fixed retarded time
items.statement:
Let the laboratory frame and SI conventions be those of the framework, and let $\rho,J$ be a jointly smooth conserved volume source supported in $\overline B_a(0)$ in space at every time, for some $a>0$. Let $E,B$ be the retarded fields generated by that source. Write $S^2=\{n\in\mathbb R^3:|n|=1\}$, $r=|x|$, and $t=u+r/c$. If maps $E_{\mathrm{rad}},B_{\mathrm{rad}}:S^2\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ satisfy

$$rE(rn,u+r/c)\longrightarrow E_{\mathrm{rad}}(n,u),\qquad rB(rn,u+r/c)\longrightarrow B_{\mathrm{rad}}(n,u)$$

uniformly in $n\in S^2$ and $u$ in every compact interval as $r\to\infty$, then $E_{\mathrm{rad}}$ and $B_{\mathrm{rad}}$ are the electric and magnetic radiation data at fixed retarded time. The scaled fields carry units $\mathrm V$ and $\mathrm T\,\mathrm m$, respectively. This definition by itself does not assert that the limits exist.
items.strategy: conditional definition; limit existence is established by the radiation theorem

references.title: Niklas Beisert, Elektrodynamik, Vorlesungsskript, ETH Zürich 2024 FS, complete 176-page course script
references.locator: §11.2–§11.3, printed pp. 11.4–11.10 (PDF pp. 124–130): the retarded-time radiation region, fixed retarded-time observation path and the distinction from near-zone and fixed-time limits.

references.title: Richard Fitzpatrick, Classical Electromagnetism: An intermediate level course, University of Texas at Austin, complete author-hosted HTML lecture notes
references.locator: Chapter 4, node 52, “Retarded fields”: the retarded-time fields, their $1/R$ radiation-zone part and the separation from the near-field terms.

items.physical_scope: Definition of the scaled far-field radiation data for the smooth retarded Maxwell branch generated by a source supported in one fixed spatial ball at every time. Uniformity is specified on the unit sphere and on compact retarded-time intervals. The definition asserts no measured radiation, no infinite-time history bound beyond the source conditions of the carrier, and no empirical or statistical claim.

items.title: Transverse far field with a uniform remainder
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Use the SI laboratory chart and source conventions: $\rho:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ has units $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ and $J:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ has units $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{-2}$. Let $a,c,\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$, and let $\rho,J$ be jointly $C^\infty$, vanish for $|y|>a$, and satisfy $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}_yJ=0$. Let $K=[u_-,u_+]\subset\mathbb R$ be a nondegenerate compact interval, $u_-<u_+$, and put $K^\sharp=[u_--2a/c,u_++2a/c]$. For $j=0,1,2$, define

$$M_{\rho,j}:=\sup_{\overline B_a\times K^\sharp}|\partial_t^j\rho|,\qquad M_{J,j}:=\sup_{\overline B_a\times K^\sharp}|\partial_t^jJ|.$$

For $n\in S^2$ and $u\in K$, define the retarded current moment and its derivative by

$$I(n,u):=\int_{B_a}J(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy,\qquad V(n,u):=\partial_u I(n,u)=\int_{B_a}J_t(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy.$$

Let $E,B$ be the selected retarded fields of the preceding theorem, set $S=E\times B/\mu_0$, and define

$$\Gamma_E:=\frac{\mu_0\lambda_3(B_a)}{4\pi}\left(4c^2M_{\rho,0}+13caM_{\rho,1}+a^2M_{\rho,2}+3aM_{J,1}+\frac{a^2}{c}M_{J,2}\right),$$

$$\Gamma_B:=\frac{\mu_0\lambda_3(B_a)}{4\pi}\left(4M_{J,0}+\frac{13a}{c}M_{J,1}+\frac{a^2}{c^2}M_{J,2}\right).$$

Then for every $n\in S^2$, $u\in K$ and $r\ge2a$, with $E_{\mathrm{lead}}(n,u,r):=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times V(n,u))$,

$$\left|E(rn,u+r/c)-E_{\mathrm{lead}}(n,u,r)\right|\le\frac{\Gamma_E}{r^2},\qquad \left|B(rn,u+r/c)-\frac{n\times E_{\mathrm{lead}}(n,u,r)}{c}\right|\le\frac{\Gamma_B}{r^2}.$$

Consequently the radiation data of the preceding definition exist uniformly on $S^2\times K$ and equal

$$E_{\mathrm{rad}}(n,u)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}n\times(n\times V(n,u)),\qquad B_{\mathrm{rad}}(n,u)=\frac{n\times E_{\mathrm{rad}}(n,u)}{c}.$$

For each fixed retarded time $u$, the outward retarded-time flux has the exact limit

$$\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S^2}r^2n\cdot S(rn,u+r/c)\,d\Omega(n)=\frac{\mu_0}{16\pi^2c}\int_{S^2}|n\times V(n,u)|^2\,d\Omega(n).$$
items.strategy: direct; differentiate the retarded potentials, use conservation to remove the longitudinal scalar-potential term, estimate each geometric and time-shift remainder uniformly, and pass the resulting uniform flux limit through the finite sphere integral.

references.title: Niklas Beisert, Elektrodynamik, Vorlesungsskript, ETH Zürich 2024 FS, complete 176-page course script
references.locator: §11.3, printed pp. 11.7–11.13 (PDF pp. 127–133): radiation-zone fields, the fixed-frequency far-field expansion, angular dipole power and the separate wavelength-versus-source-size assumption.

references.title: Richard Fitzpatrick, Classical Electromagnetism: An intermediate level course, University of Texas at Austin, complete author-hosted HTML lecture notes
references.locator: Chapter 4, node 52, “Retarded fields”: the retarded field integrals, transverse $1/R$ radiation terms, the continuity-equation cancellation and the near-zone/far-zone distinction; the uniform remainder here is proved independently.

items.physical_scope: Uniform far-field limits and retarded-time Poynting flux for smooth conserved volume sources supported in one fixed spatial ball at every time. The source may have an arbitrary smooth time history; the estimates use only stated derivative suprema on bounded retarded-time intervals. The result asserts a conditional prediction of the selected classical vacuum Maxwell model, not an empirical measurement, point-source field, self-force or radiation-reaction law.

items.title: Finite multipole expansion with an absolute dipole-power error
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the source, SI and retarded-field hypotheses of the preceding transverse-radiation theorem on a nondegenerate compact retarded-time interval $K$. Fix an integer $N\ge0$. Define the $N$th finite retarded-current Taylor coefficient by

$$\mathcal J_N(n,u):=\sum_{k=0}^{N}\frac{1}{k!\,c^k}\int_{B_a}(n\cdot y)^k\,\partial_t^{k+1}J(y,u)\,dy,$$

and define the source-scale remainder

$$\mathcal R_N(u):=\frac{a^{N+1}}{(N+1)!\,c^{N+1}}\int_{B_a}\sup_{|s-u|\le a/c}\left|\partial_t^{N+2}J(y,s)\right|\,dy.$$

The coefficient $\mathcal J_N$ and the remainder $\mathcal R_N$ both have units $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$. The supremum is finite and integrable in $y$. Let

$$A_N(u):=\sup_{n\in S^2}|\mathcal J_N(n,u)|,\qquad P(u):=\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S^2}r^2n\cdot S(rn,u+r/c)\,d\Omega(n),$$

where $P(u)$ exists by the preceding theorem. Then uniformly for $n\in S^2$ and $u\in K$,

$$|V(n,u)-\mathcal J_N(n,u)|\le\mathcal R_N(u),$$

$$\left|E(rn,u+r/c)-\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times\mathcal J_N(n,u))\right|\le\frac{\Gamma_E}{r^2}+\frac{\mu_0\mathcal R_N(u)}{4\pi r}\qquad(r\ge2a),$$

$$\left|P(u)-\frac{\mu_0}{16\pi^2c}\int_{S^2}|n\times\mathcal J_N(n,u)|^2\,d\Omega(n)\right|\le\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi c}\bigl(2A_N(u)+\mathcal R_N(u)\bigr)\mathcal R_N(u).$$

For $N=0$, $\mathcal J_0(n,u)=p''(u)$ for the time-dependent electric dipole moment $p(u):=\int_{B_a}y\rho(y,u)\,dy$, and $\mathcal R_0(u)=\frac ac\int_{B_a}\sup_{|s-u|\le a/c}|J_{tt}(y,s)|\,dy$. Consequently

$$\left|P(u)-\frac{\mu_0}{6\pi c}|p''(u)|^2\right|\le\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi c}\left(2|p''(u)|\mathcal R_0(u)+\mathcal R_0(u)^2\right).$$

Every finite truncation has its own explicit derivative remainder. No convergence of the infinite Taylor series and no relative error at an angular node are asserted.
items.strategy: identify the dipole coefficient by differentiating its source moment and integrating continuity by parts, apply vector-valued Taylor's theorem pointwise in the source position, then propagate the absolute remainder through the transverse field and power formulas.

items.physical_scope: Finite Taylor truncations of the retarded current moment and their far-field and radiated-power errors for smooth conserved volume sources supported in a fixed spatial ball. The first truncation is the electric-dipole term and has an explicit absolute source-time-variation error. No relative estimate at angular nodes, unconditional frequency or ka approximation, empirical measurement, point-source field, self-force or radiation-reaction claim is made.

title: Radiation asymptotics and controlled multipole expansion — Examples

items.title: A dipole node does not control the relative multipole error
items.statement: There are jointly smooth charge and current densities of compact support in both space and time for which the electric dipole acceleration is parallel to $n=e_3$, so the electric-dipole radiation amplitude at $n$ vanishes, while the exact retarded radiation amplitude at $n$ is nonzero. Thus an absolute source-scale error bound for the multipole expansion gives no relative error bound at a dipole node.
items.strategy: construct one smooth electric-current pulse and one smooth divergence-free circulating pulse, then evaluate their dipole and shifted-current moments in the axial direction.

references.locator: §11.3, printed pp. 11.10–11.13 (PDF pp. 130–133): the electric-dipole angular node, higher electric and magnetic multipoles, and the warning that the expansion is controlled by source-size and derivative assumptions.

items.physical_scope: A constructed smooth compact-source example in the retarded classical Maxwell model: at one direction the electric-dipole radiation vanishes while a higher source moment gives nonzero radiation. It is a conditional model example, not a measured antenna pattern or empirical claim.

items.title: The radiation limit depends on the observation-time path
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and the SI retarded Maxwell model with no independent homogeneous field. In its laboratory chart, spatial coordinates have units $\mathrm m$ and times have units $\mathrm s$. Fix $a,c>0$ with units $\mathrm m$ and $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$, a retarded time $u\in\mathbb R$, and an amplitude $\alpha>0$ with units $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-2}\,\mathrm s^{-2}$. Let $f\in C_c^\infty(B_a(0))$ be dimensionless and nonnegative with $\int f>0$, extended by zero to $\mathbb R^3$, and let $G\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$ have units $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-2}$ and equal $\alpha(t-u)^2$ on a neighborhood of $[u-a/c,u+a/c]$. Set $\rho(y,t)=-G(t)\partial_3f(y)$ and $J(y,t)=G'(t)f(y)e_3$, where $e_1=(1,0,0)$ and $e_3=(0,0,1)$. These jointly smooth maps $\rho:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ and $J:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ are conserved sources of compact space-time support, with units $\mathrm C\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ and $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{-2}$. For the direction $n=e_1$, the scaled electric field $rE(rn,u+r/c)$ has a nonzero limit. For any fixed observation time $t_f$, however, the retarded fields vanish at $x=rn$ for every sufficiently large $r$, because all source retarded times are then before the pulse.

items.physical_scope: A constructed smooth charge pulse in the retarded classical Maxwell model. At any fixed observation time its exterior field is eventually zero as the observation radius grows, while along a fixed retarded-time path the scaled electric field has a nonzero radiation-data limit. The example is conditional and contains no reported measurement.
